newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt slides with U.S. market, eyes U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt slides with U.S. market, eyes U.S. data.

text.p: Emerging debt prices dropped on Thursday with slumping U.S. Treasuries as players moved cautiously ahead of Friday's U.S. wholesale inflation data, traders said.
Brady bond traders said that most of the downside coming from inter-dealer activity, and institutional players sitting on the sidelines.

"With the Treasury market coming off brutually, the Brady market had nowhere to go but down," said one trader at a U.S. money center bank. "Dealers that are long are dragging the market down. There's no investor selling."
Most Latin American paper slumped as the benchmark T-bond gave back 22/32 to yield 6.89 percent by late afternoon.
Brazilian C bonds slipped 7/8 to 71-7/8 bid, Argentine FRBs fell 5/8 to 83-1/2 and Mexico's global bond due 2026 dropped 1-3/8 to 100-7/8.
"Brazil and Argentina both look pretty firm," another Brady dealer said. "I think they could actually outperform if you see any kind of pop or a firming in U.S. Treasury market.
The U.S. bond market slipped Thursday on a surprisingly dip in new claims for unemployment insurance, reviving signs of U.S. labor market tightness.
Debt analysts were looking September's U.S. producer prices, forecast to rise 0.3 percent, for release Friday at 0830 EDT for inflation signs.

"Everyone has been waiting all week for this number," one trader said. "I think that dealers got loaded up on the payrolls number last week on the payrolls number and the buyers never showed up to the party."
In Latin America, the main excitement focused on Venezuela, where rumors, later dismissed, of a cabinet shakeup weighed on debt prices.

Venezuelan Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff, about whom the resignation talk centered, said that the rumors could be linked to enemies of the govenrment and adversaries of the economic program inplace.
UBS Securities Debt Strategist Ingrid Iversen said Venezuela's swift knockdown of the shakeup talk reflected a sensitivity to market concerns for the Petkoff's presence.
"They know how important it is to maintain confidence and for that Petkoff is essential," Iversen said. "If the markets panic then money could flow out and could have a real impact."
Russian bond prices also fell, giving back some of their stunning recent gains along with the rest of the market.
Russian Vnesh dollar loans dropped 1-1/8 to 78-1/4, and the MinFin 3 paper lost 3/4 to 82.

Standard & Poor's, which rated Russia's long-term foreign currency debt at BB-minus, said Thursday that it would study key legal questions about Russia's support for Vnesh loans before deciding on a credit rating for that paper.
